newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes mixed amid weather jitters.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes mixed amid weather jitters.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed, with a late fall in soybeans trimming the early gains in the corn pit, traders said.
But the market was strong in early dealings and held firm into the close on concerns about seeding the U.S. corn crop, traders said.
"Last night's six- to 10-day (forecast) was friendly. It was cold and wet," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
National Weather Service's six- to 10-day outlook called for most of the U.S. Midwest to get above-normal precipitation and below-normal temperatures from April 13 through 17.
That could slow the seeding pace for U.S. corn, especially in the northern reaches of the key corn states. Farmers could choose to switch to beans away from corn.
The market was trying to consolidate after Monday's rally that was generated by the harsh weather in the upper U.S. Midwest and also fueled by a strong surge in the soybean pit.
Also, overall slow farmer selling helped underpin the market, the traders said.
Corn closed 1-1/4 cents lower to 1/4 cent higher, with May down 1-1/4 at $2.99-1/2 per bushel.

In spread trading, E.D. and F. Man International bull spread 800,000 May/July at 2-1/2 cents, premium July, traders said. Iowa Grain did 500,000 bushels of July/December at 13-3/4 to 14-1/4 cents, traders said.
In outright dealings, Smith Barney sold two million bushels of May, Dean Witter sold one million May and Cargill Inc sold 2.5 million July and sold one million bushels of May, traders said.
Prudential Securities bought three million bushels of December and Refco Inc bought 2.5 million bushels of December, the traders said.
Corn volume was estimated by CBOT at 56,000 contracts, against Monday's actual volume of 66,171 contracts.

In corn options, LFG Futures sold 400 July $2.80 puts at 4-1/4 cents, Cargill Investor Services bought 500 May $3.20 calls at 3/4 to 5/8 cent and FIMAT Futures sold 300 May $3.00 calls at 6-1/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000, below the 18,943 traded Monday.
